#image("/imgs/ap-calc-bc-2024-frq-04-diagram-01.png", width: 65%)

The graph of the differentiable function $f$, shown for $- 6 <= x <= 7$, has a horizontal tangent at $x = - 2$ and is linear for $0 <= x <= 7$. Let $R$ be the region in the second quadrant bounded by the graph of $f$, the vertical line $x = - 6$, and the $x$ - and $y$-axes. Region $R$ has area 12.

(a) The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)= integral_(0)^(x) f(t) d t$. Find the values of $g(- 6)\, g(4)$, and $g(6)$.

(b) For the function $g$ defined in part (a), find all values of $x$ in the interval $0 <= x <= 6$ at which the graph of $g$ has a critical point. Give a reason for your answer.

(c) The function $h$ is defined by $h(x)= integral_(- 6)^(x) f'(t) d t$. Find the values of $h(6)\, h'(6)$, and $h''(6)$. Show the work that leads to your answers.
